label: input h at one of the first three original positions
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter h during the original phase at steps 0-2 (every step with in_tok == h and t <= 2 is active; precision 1.0 on dev). A weak tail fires on h at step 3 (~1300 activations, ~0.1% of mass). Magnitude falls with position: h at t=0 and t=1 carry ~38% of the mass each, t=2 ~24%. Lowest-quartile examples are h at t=2 (~0.5 of max); the max (1.907) shows up at t=1, e.g. after j. A second h right after an earlier h fires more weakly (~0.55). Never fires on other tokens, on h at t >= 4, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase (including when h is being output).

issues: Minor: 'never fires in the copy phase' is off by one step. The dev split has 1 copy-phase activation (out_tok n, recall_idx 1) and 1 activation at t=4. This is negligible noise.

The t=3 tail is real but not worth adding. h at t=3 fires on only about 8% of occurrences (1309 of about 16.7k), all weak (0.02-0.10 of max). Widening to t<=3 drops test precision to 0.774 (F1 0.873, down from 0.987).

Odd scoring result: the predicate with n_seen(['h'])==0 added gets exactly the same test score as the original, even though h-after-h examples fire at 0.55. n_seen probably counts the current step. This does not affect the verdict.

Confirmed: precision 1.0 on test with 0 false positives; recall 0.974; mass recall 0.999. All activation mass is on in_tok h. Mass by step is t0 0.380, t1 0.384, t2 0.235, so magnitude falls at t=2. The max (1.907) is at t=1 after j. Lowest-quartile examples are h at t=2, around 0.5-0.6 of max. Nothing fires at the delimiter or on out_tok h.
